Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone - Season 1
Oct 28

Take on New Frontlines: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 Arrives on November 6!

Season 1: Full Intel

The hunt is on in Season 1 of Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare® 4, arriving hot on the heels of the game’s launch. Highlights include new maps and modes in Multiplayer, while in DMZ, the X01 Black Site opens up along with new enemies, orders, and more. Two new Call of Duty®: Warzone™ maps — Hajin and Zodiac — plus integration with Modern Warfare 4 round out the colossal season of content.

The Season 1 Roadmap. Includes major updates to Multiplayer, DMZ, and more.

Multiple in-game Events raise the stakes throughout the Season, including the Wager Match Event, Weapon Camo Events, a Squad Up Event, and more. Plus, expand your arsenal with new weapons including the CSG-35 SMG and the Cronen Osprey Assault Rifle. Later in the season, hunt down foes with the JAK 12 Shotgun and the ZLR Talonhawk Melee Weapon.

Get ready for a massive influx of content when Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 goes live at 0000 (midnight) ET on November 6 (2100 PT on November 5) on Steam.

Full Intel on Call of Duty: Warzone Coming Nov 2!

Play across two new maps in Call of Duty®: Warzone™ as the Season 1 update brings both Hajin and Zodiac, plus the return of Verdansk and Rebirth Island, additional game modes, gameplay features, and more as Modern Warfare 4 becomes fully integrated with the free-to-play game. Keep your eyes on the Call of Duty blog this Monday, November 2, for a separate post and Roadmap fully covering everything coming to Call of Duty: Warzone in Season 1. This blog focuses on the Season 1 Multiplayer, DMZ, and global game updates.

Modern Warfare 4: Season 1 Multiplayer Content

MULTIPLAYER CONTENT SUMMARY

More than Six Maps: Brave inclement weather across the war torn Backstab, battle amidst towering rock walls in Canyon, and drop into a reimagined Shoot House. In the Mid-Season, drop into additional new locations: Ministry, Overflow, and additional \[CLASSIFIED] maps. Plus, play Shipment now, newly added in the leadup to Season 1.

Kill Block: Crash: Drop into Kill Block where the map is static, Crash is always front and center, and additional game modes across Core MP are available.

6+ Modes: Kick off Halloween the right way with the pre-season arrival of Infected and Possession. At Season 1 launch, play the fan-favorite Grind mode, plus Drop Zone and Gauntlet 1v1 as part of the Wager Match Event. Expect more Modes arriving, starting at Mid-Season.

Multiplayer Maps

Backstab (Launch)

Brand-New, 6v6, Medium-Sized

Trek through the fallen snow of this war-torn town, where abandoned tanks litter the landscape and drone ordinance line the shelves of a deserted dwelling. Fight in the streets where long-range sightlines reign or head inside the open buildings for a closer battle.

On the ground, use the buildings and outer walls to control your sightlines. For a greater view, look to the map’s several vantage points, including the roof of the Stronghold House and the upper levels of the Sniper House, Grandpa’s House, and the Destroyed Building. Throughout the area, blasted walls create interesting flank routes. Use everything on hand to secure the win and then get out of this frostbitten battleground.

Canyon (Launch)

Brand-New, 6v6, Medium-Sized

Turn up the heat in the sun-scorched terrain of Canyon as towering rock walls trap in the chaos below. Try your luck along the River near the site of the Convoy Ambush or take the Cliff Path for its rugged vistas and winding pathways. Featuring wide open spaces interspersed with massive natural boundaries, you’ll have to time your movements to avoid getting caught without cover.

Head into the northern Cave to cool off in the shade, leading to an Abandoned Shack where hidden Operators can ambush passing enemies. Look for opportunities throughout to climb up to a higher vantage point, including small shelves and platforms as well as the central Mesa giving views toward both ends of the map.

Shoot House (Launch)

Reimagined, 6v6, Medium-Sized

Redeploy to Shoot House using the new combat and movement systems of Modern Warfare 4. While veterans of the map will instantly recognize the layout, the setting is reimagined against the rugged terrain of North Korea during a light snowfall.

Shoot House consists of three primary lanes: Fight across the southern Junkyard, through the tunnels leading toward the Center, or over and around the northern Containers. Operators seeking a dominant view will need to fight for control of the overhead Hospital and Apartment. Whichever path you take, there are plenty of interconnected routes between them, giving the savvy Operator a wide array of tactics throughout.

Season 1: Reloaded: Mid-Season Maps

Ministry: Battle erupts at the Global Peace Summit, causing damage to an embassy as Operator fight in and around the building. On this diplomatic summit, only the most aggressive policies can win.

Overflow: A convoy of mobile rocket launchers fire their projectiles in the distance on this map centered around a factory and its surrounding farmland.

Additional Maps: Expect fierce firefights across additional, remarkable locations at mid-season, and intel dropping during the Season 1 Reloaded comms.

Kill Block: Crash

It’s helicopter down as a new featured Kill Block combo arrives for Season 1. When deploying to this map, all three slabs remain static, and do not change between rounds. This set of three slabs were hand-picked by Infinity Ward based on the most popular combinations from the MW4 Beta. This also means this Crash combination is added to a variety of other playlists throughout the Core Multiplayer Modes, including Search and Destroy.

In Case You Missed It: Shipment

Shipment (Pre-Launch, October 27)

Remaster, 6v6, Small-Sized

Shipment is back! In this remastered version, the iconic map is set on a Russian harbor, hemmed in between the water and the concrete panel buildings making up the urban landscape around it. The map itself is true to form with a classic layout and appearance that players will be right at home with, enhanced by Modern Warfare 4’s visual and gameplay improvements.

Released as part of the Preseason offering shortly after launch, Shipment is now available to play. Brave the chaos and use its relentless pace of engagements to level up those crucial early Weapon ranks, so you’re ready to go when the Season 1 Multiplayer maps arrive.

Multiplayer Modes

Possession (Pre-Season: October 29)

New Mode

For the Halloween season, Possession is a fast, visceral party mode moshpit. Eliminate enemy players to possess them, transmigrating to their location and stealing their Loadout. Eliminate enemies to fly across the map to get on the Hardpoint, or to clear a Search and Destroy bombsite. But beware, you’ll always possess an eliminated enemy, so check your targets before committing to the kill.

Infected (Pre-Season: October 30)

Returning Mode

It’s Survivors vs. the Infected in this team-based party mode where one player is randomly assigned to the Infected team at the start of the match. Every time the Infected player eliminates a Survivor, that player joins the swarm of the Infected. If you’re Infected, eliminate as many as you can to bolster your ranks. If you’re a Survivor, hold out as long as you can against the hordes of Infected.

The Infected are all about speed and stealth, equipped with the FSS Carbon Edge Combat Knife, a Throwing Knife, and the Ninja Perk to assist in their shambling sneak attacks. Survivors carry heavier armaments like the Rezi 12 Shotgun with hot-loaded explosive slugs via the Enforcer Apex Attachment plus Trip Wire and a Concussion Grenade.

Infect everyone or survive the game to win.

Grind (Launch)

Returning Mode

Eliminate players, recover their dog tags, and take them to the Bank to score in Grind. There are two Bank on the map, and both teams can deposit their carried dog tags in either one. Operators can carry multiple dog tags and will drop all carried tags upon being eliminated. Swoop them up and drop them at the Bank to score big.

Drop Zone (Launch)

Returning Mode

The rich get richer in Drop Zone, where teams fight to hold a single rotating objective. Periodic airdrops deliver Killstreak packages over the Drop Zone. Open them up for random Killstreaks you can use to defend your position or to break the enemy line the next time they have control of the Drop Zone.

Gauntlet 1v1 Gunfight (Launch, LTM)

Variant Mode

Feeling confident? Throw down in the ultimate confrontation as Gauntlet 1v1 Gunfight arrives, accessible via the Wager Match Event. Wager your trophies and eliminate the enemy to secure the win. The winning player stays to face another opponent. Win multiple matches to claim the waged reward. More Modes Coming at Mid-Season.

Expect multiple additional modes at mid-season, including Counter Attack, where your focus is detonating bombs at the enemy Comm Station while protecting your own from attack. Additionally, take your foes down to the ground in a new mode that adds a twist to the Team Deathmatch formula.

And More coming via Events in the Season 1 Reloaded content drop.

Modern Warfare 4: Season 1 DMZ

DMZ CONTENT SUMMARY

Infiltrate X01: We've confirmed North Korean forces have set up shop in a former Russian facility on the edge of Hajin's borders. Designation: X01. Search the vast cargo bays and vehicle depots, descend to underground labs, production lines, and infiltrate the sealed Deep Vault. X01’s maze of tunnels and shifting hazards calls for careful planning, specialized equipment, and squad coordination.

New Orders and Threats: Ghost guides Operators through new DMZ Orders as they push deeper into X01. All further intel on the threats within this facility has been expunged from intercepted data.

New Gear, Extraction, and Events: Expect new and powerful equipment, all deemed \[CLASSIFIED]. As the facility starts to close off extraction points, complete the required steps to escape, or die trying! Also available to all DMZ Operators are Events throughout Season 1, including special Commander Hunts, and other activities with rewards well worth deploying for.

New Location: Designation X01

New DMZ Orders incoming. Announcement for all Tier One Operators within the Hajin Exclusion Zone:

A previously undiscovered weapons facility — codenamed X01 — has recently been seized by enemy forces. Recent reconnaissance along the northern border of North Korea has determined an infiltration point, allowing for deployment through Hajin. Current data suggests this facility was a GRANIT Arms black site. It appears comprised of a dimly lit, labyrinthian network of passageways, tunnels, and linking chambers surrounding a clandestine weapons assembly line and other, more surprising locations. Appearing to be fully enclosed from the outside world, ground-penetrating radar has revealed multi-floored vertical traversals, where the only reliable edge you may have is the back-up of your squadmates.

Expect heavy resistance, as intel brought back by Ghost indicates troops and specialists from the 100 Spirits NK Faction may be active in the vicinity, and it may be unwise to engage them in head-to-head combat. Stronger, more brutal entitles also patrol the interior, forcing Operators to study the available combat options before engaging.

Gear up appropriately before infil. The rogue Operator squads moving through this facility are the least of your worries. Push deeper, uncover what’s been buried here, and make your exfil. If you can.

New DMZ Orders

The Watcher for operations inside X01 is Ghost, who serves as your squad’s voice on the ground, guiding Operators through X01 as you push deeper into the facility. His updates track the route, flag emerging threats, and hint at what remains as each new area is accessed. Expect multiple pages of new DMZ Orders now that infiltrations into X01 have been sanctioned.

Additional DMZ Intel

The X01 facility holds more than we can disclose in this briefing; expect plenty to uncover on deployment, with key details deliberately withheld.

  • New Enemies: \[CLASSIFIED].

  • New Items: \[CLASSIFIED].

  • New Equipment: X01 holds equipment unavailable elsewhere, with the potential to secure rare finds on every deployment. The facility’s deeper sections may yield unfamiliar tools, valuable intel, and gear built for the threats within. What you bring out is yours to discover.

  • Escaping X01: The Facility will take extreme measures to remove intruders its forces have not been able to extricate. Make sure you always know here the nearest exfil is.

Additional FOB Enhancements and Stations

Your Forward Operating Base continues to receive improvements, both cosmetically and functionally. Here’s some of what to look for:

  • Battle Pass and Store Station: Access the Season 1 Battle Pass and BlackCell content, as well as Store Bundles, via a Station adjacent to the Survival Kit Station.

  • 3D Printer: \[CLASSIFIED].

  • Vendor: Access additional weapons and gear that you can purchase with DMZ Cash, if you’ve acquired Season 1 BlackCell.

  • Boss Board: Lieutenants: Seek additional intel on Tae-Hyun (“Knuckle”) and Chol-Min (“The Wrench”), both dangerous adversaries to encounter within your forthcoming deployments.

  • Boss Board: Commanders: Seek out toughened Commanders, including The Captain (a Juggernaut and his elite guard) and an autonomous patrolling Wheelson.

Season 1 DMZ Events

Collaborate with squad mates and take on the biggest foes across Hajin and X01 or scavenge and sell the biggest haul of valuables to acquire high-tier loot across multiple Events. Here’s what to expect in the first part of Season 1:

Threat Briefing

Intel is everything. Learn how to identify and take down DMZ’s biggest Boss threats, then exfil with unique loot to progress and earn valuable rewards like rare gear and Survival Kits. All Squad members receive credit if one of them exfils with a scavenged part from a Commander.

Threat Briefing: Battle Tank: Enter Hajin, engage a NK main battle tank in combat, removing tank parts, one per deployment. The greater the number of parts you gather over deployments, the more impressive the reward.

Threat Briefing: The Captain: Enter X01, locate and engage The Captain in combat, gathering sections of the juggernaut’s helmet, in exchange for greater rewards once you successfully exfil.

Resupply Run

Race to resupply. Track down specific items across different POIs and trade them in for high-value items like Self Revives and 3-Plate Carriers to secure your haul before anyone else.

Additional Events: Look for additional events across all game modes, and specifically some additional DMZ Threat Briefings, as Season 1 progresses.

Modern Warfare 4: General Content (MP, DMZ, WZ)

GENERAL CONTENT SUMMARY

Weapons Detail: Expand your arsenal of weapons with the arrival of the Cronen Osprey Assault Rifle and the CSG-35 SMG in the Season 1 Battle Pass. Later in the season, gain access to the full-auto JAK 12 Shotgun and the devastating melee axe known as the ZLR Talonhawk. Customize your weapons with new Attachments, including two new Apex Attachments.

Weapons Detail: Expand your arsenal of weapons with the arrival of the Cronen Osprey Assault Rifle and the CSG-35 SMG in the Season 1 Battle Pass. Later in the season, gain access to the full-auto JAK 12 Shotgun and the devastating melee axe known as the ZLR Talonhawk. Customize your weapons with new Attachments, including two new Apex Attachments.

Battle Pass and BlackCell: Progress along a 100-tier linear track in the Season 1 Battle Pass, introducing new Weapon Blueprints, Operator Skins, Calling Cards, Finishing Moves, Emotes, and more across a mix of free and premium tiers. Get the premium Battle Pass to unlock a guaranteed 50+ rewards. Purchase BlackCell, or acquire the Vault Edition and receive BlackCell content, for the ultimate experience.

Season 1 Operators: Get deeper intel on the Season 1 Operators Blix and BlackCell Agent XERO, including full bios.

C.O.D.E. Valor Pack: Call of Duty players can support veterans with the Call of Duty Endowment (C.O.D.E.) Valor Pack in Season 1 of Call of Duty®: Warzone™. Get the pack now!

Weapons Detail

Primary Weapon: Cronen Osprey (Launch)

Assault Rifle, Battle Pass Tier 16, Tier 87 Battle Pass Blueprint

Levels: 70

Rounds: 30

Reserve: 90

Fire Rate: 882 RPM

Available Criteria: Unlocked via Battle Pass.

Attachment Types: Optic, Muzzle, Barrel, Underbarrel, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, Ammunition, Magazine

Precision-engineered for relentless performance, this 5.56 rifle delivers a best-in-class fire rate without sacrificing control, accuracy, or mobility.

Rivaled only by the M4 in terms of its rate of fire, the Cronen Osprey combines speed with moderate power for an Assault Rifle that’s quick and reliable on the frontlines. In sustained fire, the weapon kicks up and to the right, though this can be countered somewhat with steady aiming and burst fire.

Apex Attachment: Cronen Helix Mk. II

A unique double-barrel receiver transforms this 5.56 rifle into a dual-fire weapon platform. Firing on both trigger pull and release, it delivers punishing damage with an unmatched rate of fire among semi-automatic weapons.

Primary Weapon: CSG-35 (Launch)

SMG, Battle Pass Tier 36, Tier 73 Battle Pass Blueprint

Levels: 42

Rounds: 28

Reserve: 112

Fire Rate: 1200 RPM

Available Criteria: Unlocked via Battle Pass.

Attachment Types: Optic, Muzzle, Underbarrel, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, Ammunition, Magazine

Featuring the highest fire rate in its class pumping out rounds at a blazing 1200 RPM, the CSG-35 excels at putting down targets fast at close ranges. Though its damage per round is only modest, the rapid accumulation of follow up shots will quickly overwhelm enemies within 20 meters. Past that distance, the weapon’s climbing recoil becomes a bit harder to control, making it difficult to stay on target. For the best results, close the distance and unleash.

Apex Attachment: CSG Crossfire

Dual-wield akimbo CSG-35 SMGs and trade accuracy for a wave of downrange chaos.

Primary Weapon: JAK 12 (In-Season)

Shotgun, Event Reward

Levels: \[CLASSIFIED]

Rounds: 8

Reserve: 16

Fire Rate: 323 RPM

Available Criteria: Unlocked via Event.

Attachment Types: Optic, Muzzle, Barrel, Underbarrel, Magazine, Rear Grip, Stock, Laser, Magazine

Devastate close-ranged targets with this full-auto Shotgun that showers foes with a cluster of pellets. Its accuracy falls off quickly, and it kicks hard after each shot, so closing the distance is required. The JAK 12 excels as a breaching tool; if you anticipate enemies on the other side of that closed door, barge through and tear them to shreds.

Apex Attachment: JAK Barrage

Launch a salvo of adhesive explosives that stick to surfaces and targets before detonating with devastating results.

Melee Weapon: ZLR Talonhawk (In-Season)

Melee, Event Reward

Levels: 10

Mastery Badges: Yes

Available Criteria: Unlocked via Event.

Attachment Types: None

Attack foes with a variety of hacks and slashes using this deadly Combat Axe, its heft capable of inflicting heavy damage to the unlucky recipients of its blade.

New: Weapon Attachments

Hyeon Auto Apex Attachment (In-Season)

Hyeon Burst Assault Rifle, Wager Match Event Reward

Converted to fully automatic fire, the Hyeon Auto was built for laying down stable, rapid fire. Offering a substantial increase in continuous RPM over the burst fire/semi-automatic variant, this weapon relies on firepower over precision.

Kastov 545 Apex Attachment (In-Season)

Kastov 762 Assault Rifle, Wager Match Event Reward

The Kastov 545 fires 5.45x39mm rounds, offering smooth handling and rapid follow-up shorts without sacrificing combat effectiveness.

M16 Burst Attachment (In-Season)

M4 Assault Rifle, Event Reward

Give the M4 the M16 treatment. Equip the M16 Burst Attachment to trade full-auto fire for controlled bursts.

Additional Attachments (In-Season)

Adjust your weapon arsenal still further with more Attachments to unlock, including the TT Iron Guard Kit for the .50 GS Pistol, and the ChainSAW Grip set for the FiNN LMG.

Season 1 Events: Initial Intel (MP, DMZ, WZ)

Season 1 kicks off with the new Wager Match Event, plus additional Events as the season progresses. Participate and unlock an impressive array of rewards including new weapons, Weapon Attachments, Weapon Blueprints, Camos, Operator Skins, and more.

Event: Wager Match (MP, DMZ, WZ)

Rewards Include: New Attachments, Operator Skin, Weapon Blueprint, Weapon Camo

Fight for top billing in the Wager Match Event*, where Trophies are the currency and collecting more of them earns valuable rewards including multiple Weapon Attachments. Enter the Gauntlet 1v1 Gunfight playlist in Multiplayer, and other challenges across DMZ and Call of Duty: Warzone.

Compete for extra rewards if you’re one of the top three winners, and Mastery Rewards to chase along the way, including an Operator Skin, Blueprint, Weapon Camo, and multiple weapon Apex Attachments.

*No money or items of real-world value are available by participating.

Additional Events (In-Season, Mid-Season, MP, DMZ, WZ)

Weapon Camo Events: Play matches to earn XP and acquire Weapon Camos.

Joint Fire Event: While you can go solo in this party up Event, there’s a big boost to your progress if you Squad Up. Bring in your Friends to activate an XP Boost that increases for larger squads, and unlock rewards including Blueprints, Charms, 2XP Tokens, a DMZ Survival Kit, and more.

Additional Events: Look for more events coming at Mid-Season.

Season 1 Battle Pass and BlackCell

Guaranteed Value and a New Streamlined Battle Pass System

The Season 1 Battle Pass is packed with 100+ Rewards, including a brand-new catch-up system that guarantees 50+ rewards in the premium Battle Pass for those who purchase it. In addition to the normal unlocking of Battle Pass content, players who fall behind in the premium Battle Pass will be automatically caught up to the Reward matching the current day of the season, up to day 50.

The Battle Pass itself is easier to navigate, too: Log in to collect your rewards and keep playing to unlock a linear 100-tier track filled with additional Operator Skins, Weapon Blueprints, Finishing Moves, Calling Cards, Weapon Charms, Reticles, and more.

Purchase the Season 1 Battle Pass for 1,100 COD Points or the Season 1 Battle Pass Bundle for 2,400 COD Points to gain access to the new catch-up system and to immediately unlock the Battle Pass Instant Rewards, including the following items:

  • Up to 1,100 COD Points

  • The “Killing Demon” Weapon Sticker

  • DMZ Survival Kit

  • New Base Weapons

  • Weapon Charms

  • Emblems

  • Calling Cards

Players who purchase the Season 1 Battle Pass and complete all 100 tiers will earn the following completion rewards:

Ultra Weapon Blueprint Tier 100 Reward

Bonus Rewards

For Season 1, there are eight additional Operator Skins you won’t want to miss! Stay tuned for more intel when the Season 1 Reloaded Blog drops.

Operators

Get more intel on Season 1 featured Operators XERO and Blix, who both excel in the art of stealth and precision.

XERO (BlackCell, Launch)

BlackCell Instant Reward

There is no record of XERO before BlackCell. Not an erased record. Not a sealed record. Nothing. The earliest known reference to him appears inside a classified BlackCell development program involving behavioral conditioning, synthetic identities, experimental combat training, and neurological augmentation.

Whether those skills were taught, implanted, or recovered from a life XERO no longer remembers remains classified. His designation originates from X-0, an internal prototype number found repeatedly throughout damaged BlackCell archives. Later documentation replaces X-0 entirely with a single name: XERO.

Field personnel describe him as unnervingly controlled. He demonstrates familiarity with locations he has supposedly never visited and occasionally recognizes people who insist they have never met him. Certain sounds, symbols, and encrypted transmissions have triggered brief episodes of memory that do not correspond with anything in his official history.

BlackCell refuses to explain them. Some within the organization believe XERO was a volunteer whose identity was deliberately erased. Others believe he was assembled from the remnants of multiple failed subjects. A more disturbing theory persists among those with access to the original program: BlackCell did not erase XERO's past. They created one where none existed.

Today, XERO operates as one of BlackCell's most closely controlled assets, deployed when an operation requires complete deniability. No country can claim him. No agency can identify him. And if BlackCell's files are accurate, XERO may not know enough about himself to ever leave them.

Blix (Battle Pass, Launch)

Battle Pass Instant Reward

A former elite operator within South Korea’s Special Warfare Command, Blix’s trajectory shifted permanently after a covert border mission led to his capture and extended imprisonment. Enduring extreme hardship, he survived the ordeal only to be funneled through a network of foreign captives and deployed into high-intensity proxy conflicts.

On the battlefield, his perspective on combat transformed into a rigid, absolute philosophy. Blix began tattooing fragments of survival codes and tactical doctrine across his skin, turning his body into a living archive of warfare. His mechanical efficiency and complete indifference to physical trauma caught the attention of the masked mercenary leader Nikto, who pulled him from the ranks to serve as a premier operative. Now deploying into the Exclusion Zone, Blix executes his objectives with silent, disciplined precision, viewing the theater of war not as a duty, but as an absolute doctrine.

Support Veterans with the Call of Duty Endowment (C.O.D.E.) Valor Pack

Call of Duty players can support veterans with the Call of Duty Endowment (C.O.D.E.) Valor Pack in Season 1 of Call of Duty®: Warzone™. Get the pack now!

Created in collaboration with U.S. Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter, the C.O.D.E. Valor Pack is inspired by his story of courage, sacrifice, and resilience. Players will discover details influenced by Kyle's military service, including his own mottos featured on in-game weapons and other elements that honor his story.

# Aim Assist Is Out of Control, Maps Feel Unbalanced — PC Players Need Better Options

I really want to enjoy Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, but the current state of controller aim assist, map design, and overall multiplayer balance is making the experience frustrating and, honestly, not very enjoyable.

**Controller Aim Assist Needs to Be Balanced**

I understand that controller players need some aim assist to compete against mouse and keyboard players. However, it feels like the aim assist in this game has gone way too far. I've had situations where I hit an enemy four to fifteen times, only for them to instantly turn around, jump around, spin nearly 180 to 360 degrees, and spray me down before I can even react.

PC players have traditionally had the advantage of precise aiming with a mouse. That advantage doesn't seem to mean much anymore when controller aim assist appears to track targets so aggressively, especially when players are constantly jumping, sliding, and spinning during gunfights.

The difference in my matches has been noticeable. I used to regularly finish games with around 40 kills and 10 deaths. Now, I'm often struggling to get 5–10 kills while dying repeatedly. I understand that not every bad match is the game's fault, but too many gunfights feel unfair and inconsistent.

There needs to be a separate PC-only matchmaking option or a serious adjustment to controller aim assist. Players who prefer mouse and keyboard should have the option to compete against others using the same input method. Crossplay can remain an option, but controller aim assist needs to be balanced so that it helps players aim without feeling like it does too much of the work for them.

**The Maps Feel Too Small and Unbalanced**

Another major problem is the map design. Too many maps feel extremely small, chaotic, and unbalanced. I would really like to see more medium-sized maps that offer a better balance between close-range combat, mid-range gunfights, and opportunities to use different playstyles.

On some of the smaller maps, you're constantly running into enemies, getting shot from multiple directions, or respawning straight back into another fight. There's barely any breathing room to reposition, use strategy, or take advantage of the equipment and perks you've unlocked.

The killstreak system is another issue. Some maps feel so small or poorly suited to certain killstreaks that using them is practically pointless. Depending on the map, there may not be enough space to use them effectively, or the layout makes them far less useful than they should be. Certain killstreaks and perks simply don't feel like they belong on some of these maps.

I'd like to see maps designed with the available perks, equipment, and killstreaks in mind. Players should be able to earn rewards and actually feel like those rewards make a difference, rather than unlocking something that is nearly useless on the map they're playing.

**There Doesn't Seem to Be Enough Map Variety**

On top of that, the overall map selection feels limited. It gets repetitive playing what feels like the same small, chaotic environments over and over again.

We need a better variety of maps, including small maps for players who enjoy fast-paced action, medium-sized maps for more balanced engagements, and larger maps where positioning, tactics, and longer-range weapons have a chance to shine.

Not every player wants to spend an entire match fighting at point-blank range. Different map sizes would give players more freedom to choose their preferred playstyle and would make multiplayer feel less repetitive.

**The Multiplayer Experience Needs Better Balance**

I'm not asking for controller players to have no aim assistance, and I'm not asking for every map to be large. I'm asking for balance, variety, and a fair playing field.

Aim assist needs to be reviewed, PC players need an input-based matchmaking option, the map pool needs more variety, and perks and killstreaks need to be useful on the maps where they're available.

I still enjoy parts of the game, which is why this is so disappointing. The potential is there, but when gunfights feel unfair and the maps are too small or poorly suited to the tools the game gives you, it takes a lot of the fun out of playing.

**My recommendation: Mixed.** The game can be fun, but the aiming balance, map design, and lack of variety are seriously hurting the multiplayer experience for me. I hope the developers take this feedback seriously and make changes that improve the game for everyone.
